module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 366

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/366](https://www.erdosproblems.com/366)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos366

/--
Are there any $2$-full $n$ such that $n+1$ is $3$-full?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_366 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 0, (2).Full n ∧ (3).Full (n + 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Note that $8$ is $3$-full and $9$ is 2-full.
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem exists_three_full_then_two_full : ∃ n > 0, (3).Full n ∧ (2).Full (n + 1) := by
  use 8
  norm_num +contextual [Nat.Full, Nat.primeFactors, Nat.primeFactorsList]

/--
Erdős and Graham asked whether $(8, 9)$ is the only pair of consecutive integers $n$, $n+1$
with $n$ $3$-full and $n+1$ $2$-full. The answer is no: $12167 = 23^3$ and
$12168 = 2^3 3^2 13^2$ is another such pair, already known to Golomb [Go70].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_366.variants.three_two :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ n > 0, (3).Full n ∧ (2).Full (n + 1) → n = 8 := by
  refine ⟨False.elim, fun h ↦ absurd (h 12167 (by norm_num) ?_) (by norm_num)⟩
  norm_num +contextual [Nat.Full, Nat.primeFactors, Nat.primeFactorsList]

/--
Are there any consecutive pairs of $3$-full integers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_366.variants.weaker : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ n > 0, (3).Full n ∧ (3).Full (n + 1) := by
  sorry


end Erdos366

reformulations.difference: The source (Erdős–Graham 1980 p. 68: 'Is n = 8 the only solution for B_3(n)=n, B_2(n+1)=n+1?'; erdosproblems.com: 'asked if this is the only pair') asks whether the solution set equals {8}; the Lean right-hand side `∀ n > 0, (3).Full n ∧ (2).Full (n + 1) → n = 8` only states that the solution set is contained in {8}, with the answer fixed to `False`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: 8 is a solution (8 = 2^3 is 3-full, 9 = 3^2 is 2-full; proved in the file by `exists_three_full_then_two_full`), so 'solution set ⊆ {8}' is equivalent to 'solution set = {8}'. `answer(False) ↔ P` asserts ¬P, i.e. some n > 0 with n ≠ 8 is a solution, which is the source's negative answer (witness 12167 = 23^3, 12168 = 2^3·3^2·13^2). I proved `{n | n > 0 ∧ (3).Full n ∧ (2).Full (n+1)} = {8} ↔ (∀ n > 0, … → n = 8)` in a scratch file.

sources_consulted: http://web.archive.org/web/20260824195540/https://www.erdosproblems.com/366 (snapshot of erdosproblems.com/366, last edited 16 July 2026; direct access blocked by Cloudflare)

https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf — Erdős & Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 68 (OCR of scanned page; subscripts verified from the image)
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf — Erdős, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions, Proc. 5th Manitoba Conf. (1976), pp. 25–44, p. 31
review.notes:
No findings. Summary of checks:
(1) Definition. `Nat.Full k n := ∀ p ∈ n.primeFactors, p^k ∣ n`. For n ≠ 0 it is equivalent to the source's 'p ∣ n ⇒ p^k ∣ n' (proved in scratch). 0 is vacuously k-full. So n = 0 would be a spurious witness for `erdos_366` and `weaker` (confirmed by #eval) and a spurious counterexample for `three_two`. All three statements carry `n > 0`. n = 1 is not a witness in any of them.
(2) Primary sources.
- Erdős–Graham 1980 p. 68 reads: 'Is it true that B_2(n)=n, B_3(n+1)=n+1 has no solution? Is n = 8 the only solution for B_3(n)=n, B_2(n+1)=n+1?' Here B_r(n) is the r-full part of n. This matches `erdos_366` and `three_two`.
- For `erdos_366`, Erdős–Graham phrase the question negatively ('has no solution?'). erdosproblems.com, the cited source, asks 'Are there any…?', and the Lean follows that phrasing verbatim. The polarity difference relative to the 1980 text is immaterial under `answer(sorry)`.
- Er76d p. 31: 'It is very probable that u^(3)_{k+1} − u^(3)_k = 1 has no solutions'. This matches `weaker`, and erdosproblems.com phrases it as 'whether there are any consecutive pairs of 3-full integers'.
(3) Computation. Using the repository's decidable instance on 1 ≤ n < 20000, and a custom enumeration of all 3-full numbers up to 10^12:
- main predicate: no witness;
- `three_two`: exactly {8, 12167};
- `weaker`: no witness.
This is consistent with the source's remarks (no other `three_two` examples below 10^22 per A060355).
(4) `answer(sorry)` prints as `True` under the repository-wide default elaborator setting (FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean). This is not specific to this file.
(5) Status.
- erdosproblems.com (snapshot 2026-08-24) records 366 as 'VERIFIABLE — Open, but could be proved with a finite example'. The teorth database also says 'verifiable'. This matches `research open` on `erdos_366` and `weaker`.
- `three_two` is correctly `research solved` with `answer(False)` and a proof.
- The teorth DB tags 366 'ambiguous statement' (last update 2025-08-31). This probably concerned older wording of the uniqueness remark. The current page is unambiguous and the file follows it.
- I could not load the erdosproblems forum thread (3 comments, '1 claimed proof') or OEIS A060355 (web.archive.org refused connections; OEIS is behind Cloudflare). The problem page itself states no solutions are claimed in the comments and still records the problem as open.
(6) Environment. I installed OCR tools (poppler-utils, tesseract, imagemagick) system-wide to read the scanned sources. Nothing under /opt/formal-conjectures was modified. The modified lakefile.toml and the run/ directory predate this session.
